newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police issue alert for tug-of-love baby.
newsitem.headline: S.African police issue alert for tug-of-love baby.

text.p: South African police have issued an alert after a tug-of-love baby adopted soon after birth was reportedly kidnapped by two men in Malawi on Saturday.
"We have put out an alert. Photographs of the child are being made as we speak and will be sent to the border posts," police spokeswoman Sharon Schutte told Reuters.
The 14-month-old baby's birth mother was distraught after hearing of the child's disappearance from the adoptive parents.
Classical musician Adri Naude, highly emotional in a state radio broadcast, said baby Timothy was kidnapped by two men who ran off with him into the mountains near Blantyre.

"I don't care what anybody does to me but leave my child alone," she said on radio. "I will kill whoever is involved in this thing. I really feel very strongly about it and they must not do anything to harm my baby at all."

The child's birth father, Laurie Fraser, has waged a lengthy court battle for the right to raise his son as a single father. Their marriage plans went awry and Naude later agreed to their baby's adoption without his consent.
South African police said they believed baby Timothy was still in Malawi, but added that reports from Blantyre were coming in very slowly.

"We were notified by the family and contacted Malawi police via Interpol. We haven't actually been informed officially by the police in Malawi but we'll do everything possible from our side to ensure the baby is safe," Schutte added.
Fraser went to South Africa's most powerful judicial authority, the 11-judge Constitutional Court, to try and gain the right to raise his son.
The court ruled in a landmark decision that single fathers should be allowed to have a say in their children's adoptions and gave legislators two years to introduce it into law.
Fraser said after the ruling he would return to the Supreme (high) Court to press his case.
